question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental quantity in the SI system?
solution:
The Correct Answer is Force

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A set of physical quantities which cannot be expressed in terms of any other quantities are known as fundamental quantities.
 
• Eg. Length, Mass, Time.
 
• Their corresponding units are called fundamental units.
 
• There are seven fundamental physical quantities in SI Units (System of International Units).
 
•

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__Derived quantities

 
• All other physical quantities which can be obtained by multiplying, dividing or by mathematically combining the fundamental quantities are known as derived quantities.
 
• Eg. Area and volume. Their corresponding units are called derived units.
